newsitem.title: USA: Mid-America Bancorp Q1 shr $0.47 vs $0.45.
newsitem.headline: Mid-America Bancorp Q1 shr $0.47 vs $0.45.

text.p: (Per share data for 1996 has been adjusted for the 3% stock dividend declared November 18, 1996.)
Excluding the effect of securities gains of $76,000 in 1997 and $1,168,000 in 1996, net income for the quarter ended March 31, 1997 increased 25.6% compared to the first quarter of last year.

The company's results for the quarter ended March 31, 1997 compared to the first quarter of 1996 reflected an increase net interest income of $1,063,000 resulting primarily from an increase in average earning assets of $111 million or 9%.

Included in the increase in average earning assets are increases in commercial and retail loans of $21 million and $27 million, respectively. The earning asset growth was funded by a $27 million increase in checking and savings account balances, a $26 million increase in time deposits and a $44 million increase in customer repurchase agreements.

The company also posted a 7.2% increase in non-interest income, excluding securities gains. This increase was achieved despite the 30% decline in money order fees resulting from the reduced agent base subsequent to the Western Union program agent base sale in the third quarter of 1996. The increase was primarily achieved from increased fees and other revenues from an expanding retail customer base, and fees from new products and services. Also, a $117,000 gain on the sale of a closed branch facility contributed to the increase in non- interest income.

The level of operating expenses in 1997 was effected by a reduction in full-time equivalent employees from 660 in March 1996 to 618 in March 1997. The company also had increases in operating expenses related to advertising and supply costs.
The return on average assets (ROA) for the three months ended March 31, 1997 was 1.32%, compared to 1.35% for the same period in 1996.

The return on average shareholder's equity (ROE) was 12.96% in the first quarter of 1997, compared to 12.99% in the first quarter of 1996. On the basis of net income excluding security gains, these performance ratios reflected significant improvement.
On he basis of "core" earnings, ROA was 1.31% in 1997 compared to 1.11% in 1996 and ROE was 12.82% in 1997 compared to 10.68% in 1996.

The allowance for loan losses was $9,097,000 on March 31, 1997, and was 1.16% of loans at the end of the first quarter. The allowance for loan losses was 234% of non-performing loans at March 31, 1997. Non-performing loans were $3.9 million and .50% of loans outstanding at March 31, 1997, compared to $4.3 million and .54% at December 31, 1996.

Other real estate aggregated $9.6 million at March 31, 1997 and was principally comprised of properties acquired in settlement of problem real estate development loans in April 1996. The real estate associated with the above mentioned problem loan situation which aggregated $15.2 million originally, has been reduced by property sales and has a carrying value of $9.4 million at March 31, 1997. The company has a contract for additional property sales expected to close in May 1997 that will further reduce the carrying value by approximately $500,000. Also, the company has a sales contract for a portion of these properties with a carrying value of approximately $1.5 million, that is contingent on zoning changes which are not expected to be resolved until late 1997.
